title.narrative: Strengthening Social Cohesion through Peacebuilding and Livelihood Interventions among Youths

description.narrative:
Jos and the wider Plateau State have, for years, grappled with recurring episodes of ethno-religious conflict, youth unemployment, and social disintegration. The state’s population is predominantly agrarian, yet youth involvement in agriculture remains limited due to lack of capacity, access to capital, land, and modern agribusiness opportunities.
Given the fragile peace and the urgent need for sustainable youth engagement and empowerment, this project will be taking to scale, leveraging on the CA Code 1 existing agribusiness project targeted at Women and youths in Plateau State to improve livelihood, social cohesion, and peacebuilding among youths in Plateau State. This project is timely, and contextually responds to National Livelihood and Social Cohesion Policy Framework, Plateau State Government Peacebuilding Agency’s strategy for youth engagement and economic inclusion, and contributes to SDGs 1 (No Poverty), 2 (Zero Hunger), 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), and 16 (Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions).
The agribusiness project, strategically designed with livelihood, social cohesion, and peacebuilding as entry points, offers a sustainable, locally appropriate, and scalable approach to youth empowerment and conflict transformation in Jos, Plateau State. Beyond income generation, it promotes inter-group collaboration, peace advocacy, and resilient community development, contributing to the long-term stabilization and prosperity of the region. This project will be implemented by a consortium of CA national partners – Social Justice and Human Development for Peace Initiative (JDPC), Jos, Christian Council of Nigeria (CCN) and Women and Children in Support of Community Development Initiatives (WOCCI).
